[LMU Open Science Center](https://www.osc.lmu.de/). [https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-research-principles/github](https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-research-principles/github)
:::

**Welcome!** This workshop is intended to introduce learners to the **essential skills** for **collaborating on shared projects** using **GitHub and RStudio**. It will guide learners step‑by‑step through the core parts of a collaborative **GitHub workflow**, including how to navigate GitHub’s interface, fork and clone repositories to work locally, and use **Git commands to commit, push, and pull changes**. Simultaneously, this workshop prepares learners to actively use reproducible research practices and how to **design a simple collaborative workflow** that keeps everyone’s work synchronized and traceable.

### Who are these materials for?

- **Educators** in higher education with or without familiarity with open research planning to **teach open research novices**
- **Self-learners** with no or limited familiarity with open research planning to **develop and build** up on their open research skills

### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;">
| Prerequisite | Description | Where to find it |
|---|---|---|
| R and RStudio installed | Latest versions of both R and RStudio | [Download RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) |
| Basic R skills | Introduction to R - Part I | [Access here]() |
| Advanced R skills | Introduction to R - Part II | [Access here]() |
| Basic Git skills | Introduction to version control with Git in RStudio | [Access here]() |
| GitHub account | Your own GitHub account | [Join GitHub](https://github.com/join) |
| Practice GitHub repo | Fork the [LMU OSC Collaborative-RStudio-GitHub repository](https://github.com/lmu-osc/Collaborative-RStudio-GitHub/tree/main) to set up a practice repository for the exercises in this lesson | |
</div>

### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you or your learners will be able to ...

- **Navigate** GitHub to collaborate on shared projects.
- **Fork** and **clone** repositories to work locally without altering the main branch.
- **Commit**, **push**, and **pull** changes to keep your project tracked and synchronized.
- **Design** a collaborative workflow that enhances the openness and reproducibility of your own projects.
